newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Russia sign accords on space, taxes, food.
newsitem.headline: France, Russia sign accords on space, taxes, food.

text.p: France and Russia signed bilateral agreements on taxes, space exploration and food production on Tuesday following wide-ranging talks on economic matters, ministers of both governments said.

All three accords were signed at a news briefing in Paris by French Prime Minister Alain Juppe and his Russian counterpart Viktor Chernomyrdin following a meeting of a Franco-Russian commission on economic relations.
The tax accord was intended to eliminate double taxation and improve cooperation against fraud, they said.
"This accord will enable us to resolve a great number of difficulties for our businesses," Chernomyrdin told reporters.

The agreement on space provided for greater cooperation between Moscow and Paris in the peaceful exploitation of space, in such realms as exploration, telecommunication and navigation, officials said.
Under the third accord, Paris and Moscow agreed to set up a joint commission on agriculture and food production.

The panel will conduct negotiations on a variety of matters of common concern including the protection of intellectual property, health checks on meat animals being shipped across borders and the licensing and certification of food products.
